Fit a list of specifications

Source: R/fit_spec.R
run_specs.Rd

Fits each specification with fit_spec(), in order. A specification that cannot be fitted (too few donors, a too-short window) is reported and skipped, and the rest carry on.

Usage

run_specs(
  specs,
  panel,
  store = NULL,
  keep = c("all", "est", "none"),
  seed_each = TRUE,
  progress = TRUE
)

Arguments

specs

A list of sdid_spec()s, for example from read_specs().

panel

An sdid_panel().

store

Directory of a run store to save into, or NULL.

keep

How much of the fit to retain: "all" (default) keeps the fitted object and every placebo draw, which every plot needs; "est" keeps only the fitted object; "none" keeps the summary alone.

seed_each

Seed each fit with seed_for(), so every specification's standard error is reproducible on its own. FALSE inherits one stream across the whole sweep instead, so a result depends on its position.

progress

Print one line per fitted specification.

Value

A list of sdid_runs, with NULL for specifications that failed.

Examples

# \donttest{
specs <- list(
  sdid_spec(label = "SDID", inference = list(replications = 30)),
  sdid_spec(label = "SC", estimator = "sc", inference = list(replications = 30))
)
runs <- run_specs(specs, prop99_panel())
#> ✔ 1/2 SDID: ATT -15.6, SE 9.55
#> ✔ 2/2 SC: ATT -19.62, SE 8.25
sdid_results_table(runs)
#>   label estimator        outcome    treated treat_time    window N0 T0    ATT
#> 1  SDID      sdid PacksPerCapita California       1989 1970-2000 38 19 -15.60
#> 2    SC        sc PacksPerCapita California       1989 1970-2000 38 19 -19.62
#>     SE     t  ci_lo  ci_hi trend_rmse placebos    spec_hash
#> 1 9.55 -1.63 -34.32  3.115       1.73    30/30 8dc336c466ef
#> 2 8.25 -2.38 -35.78 -3.459       1.66    29/30 3ed8e77dff0b
# }
